title: promote-latest.mjs fails the run on npm read lag after every write succeeded, so the GitHub Release is left uncut (paired with quest-cli QCLI-465)
description:
Twin of quest-cli QCLI-465 (opum-ai/quest-cli#530), filed the way LCLI-621/QCLI-400 were paired. Found by the 0.13.0 promotion (LCLI-665) on 2026-10-07.

promote-latest.mjs moved every dist-tag — the six platforms by dist-tag, and the launcher published onto latest from opum-ai-lore-0.13.0.tgz — and then its own post-write verification failed the run at exit 1 while npm read lag was still resolving, printing: "@opum-ai/lore: latest reads 0.12.0, expected 0.13.0" and "The writes returned success but the registry does not serve latest = 0.13.0 everywhere after 10 reads." The writes were CORRECT — the orchestrator read the registry minutes later and latest was 0.13.0 on all seven, with the launcher dist.integrity and shasum identical to the final tarball from that run — but the process had already exited 1.

Because that verification sits before them, two steps never ran: ensureGitHubRelease (the GitHub Release had to be repaired out of band, and the repair then failed on an upstream HTTP 500) and the README read-back. The record file scripts/release-0.13.0/latest-rollback.json was written and was not used.

The fix shape is the one quest-cli adopted: the post-write verification should WAIT OUT registry read lag the way the README read-back already does, instead of failing the run on a transient read. Worth deciding too: whether a read-lag failure should exit 3 (promotion complete, a post-latest step outstanding) rather than 1, which now reads as a failed promotion when the promotion in fact succeeded.

acceptanceCriteria.text: promote-latest.mjs waits out registry read lag in its post-write verification, so a promotion whose writes all succeeded completes in one run rather than exiting 1 while the npm read API catches up
On a run whose writes all succeeded, the GitHub Release is cut by ensureGitHubRelease and the README read-back runs, with neither left to an out-of-band repair

implementationNotes: SECOND WAY THE RELEASE STEP IS LEFT UNCUT (team-lead, 2026-10-07). The out-of-band repair is itself fallible. node scripts/github-release.mjs --version 0.13.0 --create returned exit 1 with "could not create release v0.13.0: HTTP 500 (https://api.github.com/repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/releases)", and nothing was created: gh release view v0.13.0 says "release not found" and v0.12.0 is still Latest. So as of this writing the 0.13.0 GitHub Release is still uncut, for the second reason. The 500 is upstream and not the payload: GitHub was partly degraded from about 15:07Z, with check-runs and commit-status returning 500 in other repositories too while release listing still worked, and the same outage later rejected a git push with "remote rejected (Internal Server Error)". The promote preflight had accepted the identical inputs minutes earlier, saying it would create release v0.13.0 "Lore CLI 0.13.0" (11887 bytes of notes), marked latest. Worth weighing when this task is fixed: a single read-lag failure should not require an out-of-band repair whose own failure mode ALSO leaves the release uncut, and the repair is not retried automatically.
